MOLECULAR CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine

PATIENT: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
SPECIMEN ID: [redacted ID]
ORDERING PHYSICIAN: Dr. [redacted name]
DATE COLLECTED: [redacted date]
DATE REPORTED: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Abdominal mass; histopathology consistent with Burkitt's lymphoma

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) for IGH/MYC Rearrangement

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue sections using the ProbeMax IGH/MYC/CEP8 triple color dual fusion probe set. This probe combination detects the t(8;14)(q24;q32) translocation characteristic of Burkitt's lymphoma.

Probe specifications:
- IGH (14q32): Green fluorophore
- MYC (8q24): Red fluorophore  
- CEP8 (Chromosome 8 centromere): Aqua fluorophore

A minimum of 200 interphase nuclei were analyzed from the infiltrated tissue region.

RESULT: ABNORMAL

IGH/MYC [t(8;14)] rearrangement DETECTED

FISH Pattern Analysis:
- Normal pattern (2R2G2A): 15% of cells
- Abnormal pattern (1R1G2F2A): 85% of cells

The abnormal signal pattern showing one red (MYC), one green (IGH), two fusion (IGH/MYC), and two aqua (CEP8) signals is consistent with the presence of t(8;14)(q24;q32) translocation.

INTERPRETATION
The detection of IGH/MYC rearrangement in 85% of analyzed cells confirms the presence of t(8;14)(q24;q32), the hallmark cytogenetic abnormality of Burkitt's lymphoma. This finding supports the histopathologic diagnosis and is consistent with the clinical presentation of an abdominal mass.

The t(8;14) translocation juxtaposes the MYC oncogene with the immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGH) locus, resulting in constitutive MYC expression and aggressive B-cell proliferation characteristic of Burkitt's lymphoma.

CLINICAL CORRELATION
This molecular cytogenetic finding confirms the diagnosis of Burkitt's lymphoma. The high percentage of cells with the translocation indicates a clonal neoplastic process.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
